relevance_note: A cross-sectional NIH cohort study of nine autoinflammatory diseases. It includes 'HA20 (n=14)' patients with TNFAIP3 disease-causing variants, but reports them only as aggregate percentages and counts: no patient labels, variant descriptions or per-patient phenotypes.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; no table was script-transcribed. HA20 data are cohort-level only (Table 1: age, sex percentage and treatment percentages; Table 2: urticaria prevalence; figures). Two anonymous single-patient mentions exist: 'eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EGE) was diagnosed in 2 patients (HA20 and HIDS)' and 'perioral swelling temporally associated with flare was reported by ... one patient each with DADA2, HA20, and CANDLE'. Neither has a label, variant or other individual detail, and the two cannot be told apart or linked, so no individual rows were created. Following the instructions for papers without patient-level detail, the flag is false and the patient tables are empty. Contradictions in the paper (none affect the HA20 count): cohort sizes differ between the text and Table 1 (FMF n=118 vs 117 identified; TRAPS n=73 vs 72; HIDS n=38 vs 39); protocol numbers differ between Methods and Results/Ethics (94-HG-0104 vs 94-HG-0105; 10-I-0148 vs 10-I-1048); HA20 'Sex (% M) 30.8%' is not a whole-number fraction of 14 (it equals 4/13), which suggests a denominator of 13. The paper does not state that any patients were described in earlier publications.

year.span: Journal: Annals of the rheumatic diseases (2021)

study_type.span: In this cross-sectional study, clinical data were assessed in 425 AID patients using questionnaires and chart reviews.

span: Smaller cohorts with PAPA (n=18), HA20 (n=14), CANDLE (n=14), and SAVI (n=12) were also followed.
All patients carried a molecular diagnosis of MEFV, NLRP3, TNFRSF1A, ADA2, MVK, PSTPIP1, TNFAIP3, proteasome genes, or STING1 disease-causing variants
